defect: Anchor occurrences are counted overlapping, so an anchor the defect catalog counts once is refused as occurring more than once.
A line break in an anchor matches only LF, so every multi-line anchor in a file checked out with CRLF reads as missing.
An anchor written with CRLF line breaks is matched as written, so it reads as missing in a file with LF line breaks.
An anchor's regular-expression characters are not escaped, so an anchor holding a dot or brackets matches other text or none.
An anchor that occurs more than once is replaced at its first occurrence, so the mutation lands on a site the author may not have meant.
A replacement is written with its own LF line breaks into a CRLF match, so the mutated text mixes line endings.
A match with no line break of its own is taken to use LF, so a line the replacement adds to a CRLF file ends with LF.
The probe is placed at the whole replaced text rather than the part that changed, so it fires where the changed code never ran.

defect: A call's callee takes a probe, so a method called through the wrap loses its receiver and the probe changes what the module does.
A change under a TypeScript value wrapper is judged at the wrapper's operand slot, so it gets no probe site and its experiment never runs.
A block's statement list takes no probe statement, so a replaced statement in a function body gets no probe site.
A hoisted function declaration takes a probe statement before it, which fires when the module loads, marking every test reached though the function never ran.
A `typeof` operand is wrapped, so `typeof` of an undeclared name throws a ReferenceError and the probe fails a test.
A link of an optional chain is wrapped, ending the chain there, so a short circuit that returned undefined now throws a TypeError.
A wrap that opens a statement after a line with no semicolon is written bare, so it parses as a call of the previous line's value.
A failed parse reports no offset, so a mutation whose text does not parse is refused without saying where the parse failed.
Code inside an ambient declaration takes a probe, so a change there reads as a site that can run though its code never does.
The mutated file is keyed by the path the job was given rather than its real path, so under a consumer root reached through a link the mutation is never applied.
A firing during a test is marked on its file rather than on the test, so a test that executed the site reads not executed.
A test the reach setup file only observed reads executed in the test, so a sibling that failed without reaching the site is credited with reach.
A site executed while the test file loaded is not credited to the file's tests, though each can read what that code set.
A site executed in a suite's beforeAll is not credited to that suite's tests, though each can read what the hook set.
A site executed in one suite's beforeAll is recorded for the whole file, marking tests of other suites that never ran it.
A test the reach recorder never observed reads not executed, where reach is unknown.
A test whose afterEach threw stays marked running, so a site a later suite's beforeAll executes is credited to it as reached in the test.
A site executed while two tests run concurrently is credited to one of them, though Vitest cannot say which one ran it.
A module cached from text its file no longer holds is kept, so a run after a source edit reads the old transform.
A transform that finds the anchor other than once records nothing, so the experiment reads as though its module was never loaded.
Only the root's Vite server is wrapped, so a project with its own config file is served its module unmutated.
The mutated file is not invalidated before its experiment, so the experiment is served the baseline's cached transform and its mutation never runs.
Ending an experiment leaves its mutation active, so the restored baseline is served the last experiment's mutation.
The workspace's isolate: false is kept, so test files share a worker and a test passes or fails through another file's side effects.
The workspace's bail is kept, so an experiment whose mutation fails a test is cancelled and reads interrupted.
A run's record takes every module runTestSpecifications returns, so an experiment carries the modules and results earlier runs left.
A serialized error is reduced to its message, so the constructor marker and assertion context that tell an assertion from another failure are lost.
new: if (isPlainObject(error)) return { message: String((error as { message?: unknown }).message) };

defect: The hook states Vitest recorded on a test's result are dropped, so a failure in a hook cannot be told from one in the test body.
Suite errors are dropped, so a failed beforeAll leaves no error on the module's record.
A run's unhandled errors are reduced to text, losing the name and fields Vitest serialized.
An experiment runs though its intended test failed the baseline, so a failure the mutation did not cause can read as a detection.
The intended test is found in the baseline by its name alone, so an experiment runs against a same-named test the baseline passed in another suite.
An intended test's module is matched by project alone, so a test in no module is run against another module of its project.
An unreadable mutated file throws out of the job, so every other experiment of the workspace is lost.
An experiment whose anchor does not occur exactly once when the job starts is run anyway, spending a run on a mutation that cannot apply.
An experiment whose change has no probe site is run anyway, and its record never names the position the author must move the mutation from.
The forks pool is left to copy each transformed module to the OS temp directory, so the mutated text is written to disk.
On Vitest 4.1 the experimental module cache setting is not read, so a project that keeps the cache on has the mutated transform written under the consumer's tree.
On Vitest 5 the deprecated experimental module cache setting is read though the override has turned the cache off, so the workspace is refused and never falsified.
A bigint in a serialized error is kept as a bigint, so the job's reply cannot be sent over the executor's JSON channel and the job's record is lost.
A falsification job whose executor process died is returned as ended, with no record, as though the job had finished.
old:
return reply.type === "falsified"
      ? { ended: true, value: reply.job }
new:
return reply.type === "falsified" || reply.type === "exited"
      ? { ended: true, value: reply.job }

defect: An experiment an abort interrupted is kept in the reply as a run that finished, and the job goes on to a restored baseline.
A module Vite soft-invalidated, whose old transform it keeps and serves again, does not count as cached, so an importer of an invalidated module that was edited on disk is served from its old text.

A module of the mutated file whose transform is still running, so it holds no cached result, is not invalidated, and the mutated transform is cached after the guard has looked and served to the next run.

defect: A changed arrow function is wrapped where it is defined, so the probe fires when the module loads and marks tests that never called the function.
A `delete` operand is wrapped, so the property is never deleted and the probe changes what the module does.
A probe the parser rejects is served, so the mutated module fails to load in its experiment instead of being recorded with no probe site before any run.
In a CRLF file the end of the replacement is measured from its LF length, so a multi-line replacement's changed span stops short and its probe is refused or placed for less than the change.
An empty anchor is counted at every position of the text, so on an empty file it counts once and a replacement is applied.
An abort during the baseline leaves the planned experiments with no record, so the reply does not say they were interrupted.
An abort that arrived before the job's turn is ignored, so the job still loads the workspace's config and runs its code.
An error raised in the executor's own process is recorded without its name and message.

defect: A baseline's unhandled error that counts against the experiment is not read, so a detection stands though the baseline its test passed in leaked an error.
How a baseline ended is not read, so a detection stands on a baseline whose workers were force-stopped.
The judge does not read whether the baseline passed the test, so an experiment that ran against a test the baseline failed is credited as a detection.
The baseline-not-passed reason carries the test's state without its mode, so a test declared with it.skip cannot be told from one skipped at run time.
The restored baseline's result for the test is not read, so a detection stands though the test no longer passes unmutated.
The restored baseline's unhandled errors and ending are not read, so a detection stands though the restored baseline leaked an error that counts against it.
A restored baseline that started and left no record is read as one that failed the test, so an experiment its job did not finish reads invalid experiment where it has no verdict.
A confirming run that left no record is passed over and the first run judged in its place, so a would-be detection that never repeated gets a verdict.
How an experiment's run ended is not read, so a run that was interrupted, force-stopped or failed to cancel is judged as a whole run.
A test with no recorded beforeEach state reads as one whose hooks all passed, so a Vitest that stopped recording hook states would credit a failure in a beforeEach as a detection.
A passed test reads survived before its hook states are read, so a test whose hook states were not recorded reads as a survivor.
A failed test that holds no error counts as holding only assertion errors, so a failure with no assertion behind it is a would-be detection.
A passed test beside an unhandled error in its own run is not read as a survivor, so a mutation the test let through reads unclear.
A run started next that left no record is read as a clean one, so a detection stands though a late unhandled error may have been lost with that run.
The job's own unhandled errors and its close are not read, so a detection stands though the executor's thread raised an error or the instance failed to close.
Reach is read before the hook states, so a test whose beforeEach failed before the site could execute reads site not executed, hiding the hook that failed.
The run's unhandled error is read before the kind of the test's errors, so a test that threw a TypeError beside a leaked rejection reads unhandled error where its own error is no assertion.
A mutated module that was transformed with the anchor occurring other than once reads as never transformed, so the reason loses the count that tells the author the anchor went stale.
A baseline's unhandled error that names no test module counts against no experiment, so a detection stands beside an error no module can be blamed for.
An experiment whose run started and left no record is passed over as the run started next, so the detection before it is read against a later run though a late error may have been lost.
A run the stale-transform guard refused counts as a started run that left no record, so the detection before it reads unclear though no run started.
A record is judged against the experiment at its position whatever defect it names, so one defect's run is read with another defect's test.
A declared assertion error name matches any error whose name contains it, so an error of another name is credited as an assertion.
The executor process drops the assertion error names its request carries, so an error the consumer declared as an assertion reads as another kind and its experiment as unclear.
Every unhandled error of a baseline counts against every experiment, whatever test module it names, so one module's leak makes every defect of the workspace an invalid experiment.
A baseline's unhandled error that names the experiment's own test module is not counted against it, so the experiment is judged as though its baseline were clean.
The unhandled errors of the run started next are not read, so a detection stands though a late error of its own run may have landed in the run after it.
The confirming run's reading is not compared, so a failure that did not repeat is credited as a detection.
Every experiment that ran is run a second time, not only one whose run would be a detection, so a job runs its survivors and invalid experiments twice.
An unhandled error is recorded as naming every test module of its run, so one module's leak counts against every experiment of the job.
An unhandled error names only the first project that runs its file, so the same file's experiments under another project read the baseline as clean.
An error's fact carries its message, so the text of an assertion, which can quote source and values, reaches the facts a judgement is stored with.

defect: The falsifier version is not raised, so evidence recorded before an experiment record held its mutation file's digest is kept as current.
A job that ran nothing carries an empty list of judgements, so it reads as a job that judged every experiment it was given.

A confirming run an abort interrupted is kept as a run that finished, so the reply holds the record of a run cut short, and the experiment's missing verdict is put down to the restored baseline where its confirming run is what did not finish.
The anchor-count reason carries a count of zero whatever the anchor's count was, so an anchor that occurs twice reads as one that is missing.
The canary file names detected for the canary whose test passes after executing the site, so the set vouches for a Vitest on which a passing test is credited.
An error Vitest serialized with the name AssertionError is not read as an assertion, so a plain expect failure reads unclear.
The failure of a matcher added by expect.extend is not read as an assertion, so a jest-dom style matcher's rejection reads unclear.
The assertion error names the job was given are not read, so an error the consumer declared as an assertion reads as another kind.
A site executed outside the test, while its module loaded, reads not executed, so a test that rejects what load-time code built can never detect its mutation.
A hook state other than pass is not read, so an assertion that failed in a beforeEach is credited as a detection and a thrown afterEach reads as a failure of the body.
A suite's error is not read, so a test its failing beforeAll skipped reads as a test that did not run, with no suite named.
A module's own errors are not read, so a mutated module that threw while it loaded reads as a test absent from the run.
A reach of not executed is read as executed, so a test that failed an assertion without running the mutated site is credited as a detection and one that passed reads as a survivor.
A reach that is unknown is read as executed, so the failure of a test that ran beside others is credited though no probe says it ran the site.
The kind of a failed test's errors is not read, so a thrown TypeError, a timeout, an assertion count failure, a snapshot mismatch or an undeclared error is credited as a detection.
One assertion error is enough for a detection, so a test that also threw an error of another kind is credited though its failure may be a setup failure carried over a retry.
An unhandled error in the experiment's own run is not read, so an assertion failure beside a leaked rejection is credited as a detection.
An experiment whose run left no record reads invalid experiment, as a change with no probe site, so the author is told to fix a definition a failed run says nothing about.

A failed test that declares repeats is read as any failed test, so an assertion that failed in a beforeEach or afterEach on an earlier repeat, its last repeat's hooks and body passing, is credited as a detection.
A passed test that declares repeats reads invalid experiment, so a mutation that every repeat let through is not reported as a survivor.

defect: The repeats a test declares are not carried from the record to the facts, so the judge reads a failed repeated test as any failed test.
The job's own unhandled errors count as none in the facts, so a detection stands though the executor's thread raised an error.
The instance reads closed in the facts whatever its close error, so a detection stands though the instance failed to close.
A run's force-stop is not carried from the record to the facts, so a run whose workers Vitest force-stopped is judged as one that ended cleanly.
A run's cancel error is not carried from the record to the facts, so a run whose cancel raised an error is judged as one that ended cleanly.
How a run's execution ended is not carried from the record to the facts, so a run something interrupted is judged as one that completed.

Baseline trouble is read before whether the experiment has a verdict, so an experiment of a job that left no restored baseline, or whose confirming run left no record, reads invalid experiment where it has no verdict.
The repeats Vitest was told to give a test are not recorded, so a test its suite repeats, whose setup assertion failed on an earlier repeat alone, is credited as a detection.
A test told to run once more than once is recorded as a test Vitest runs once, so the fewest repeats a test can declare escape the reading and its hook failure is credited as a detection.
old: return repeats !== undefined && repeats > 0 ? repeats : undefined;
new: return repeats !== undefined && repeats > 1 ? repeats : undefined;

defect: The unhandled errors the job's own thread recorded are not handed to the judging, so a detection stands though the executor's thread raised an error while the instance was open.
The record of an experiment that ran carries no digest of its mutation file's text, so a detection has nothing to bind to and cannot be stored as evidence.

The record of an experiment decided without a run carries no digest though the job read its file, so a verdict such as invalid experiment for no probe site or no module has nothing to bind to and cannot be stored.
The record of an experiment whose mutation file could not be read carries a digest, so it reads as bound to a text the job never read.

The digest is taken from the mutation file as it reads when the job's records are collected, so a file edited mid-job carries the digest of the edited text, and evidence planned from the old text reads current.
The digest is taken of the text with its byte order mark dropped, so a file that starts with one never digests as a query reads it and its evidence reads stale forever.
old: return { read: true, text, digest: wholeDigest(text) };
new: return { read: true, text, digest: wholeDigest(text.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? text.slice(1) : text) };
